engine/processor.py:R5:RowProcessor:_rec: Nominal isinstance narrowing on an ELSPETH-owned exception union. _record_flush_violation takes `violation: DeclarationContractViolation | PluginContractViolation | AggregateDeclarationContractViolation` (src/elspeth/engine/processor.py:1469), fed by the three except arms of _cross_check_flush_output at processor.py:1451, :1455 and :1459. Every member is a class ELSPETH defines in src/elspeth/contracts/errors.py, so ADR-032's 'nominally type what ELSPETH owns' applies directly: this is dispatch over an owned closed union, not a parse of external data, and nothing here reads attacker- or plugin-controlled bytes. The narrowing exists because only PassThroughContractViolation (contracts/errors.py:1694, a DeclarationContractViolation subclass) carries `divergence_set` — the input fields a passes_through_input=True transform dropped. That set is folded into `violation_summary` and therefore into compute_error_hash at processor.py:1489, so two different pass-through divergences produce distinct error_hash values on the per-token FAILED rows written for every buffered token in the loop below; the generic arm can only hash the class name plus the transform name and would collapse them into one hash. isinstance rather than `type(violation) is` is required on purpose: a future subclass of PassThroughContractViolation must inherit the divergence-aware summary rather than silently fall through to the generic arm. INVALIDATED BY: `divergence_set` moving onto a common base of all three union members (the narrowing would then be unnecessary and the site should be deleted, not re-justified); the parameter union widening to admit a type ELSPETH does not define; or violation_summary no longer feeding compute_error_hash, which is what makes the distinction observable in the audit trail.
engine/processor.py:R5:RowProcessor:_exe: isinstance on a builtin exception class inside the `is_retryable` predicate, and the ordering is the point. is_retryable is declared `Callable[[BaseException], bool]` (src/elspeth/engine/retry.py:76) and handed to tenacity at retry.py:136; a predicate whose only parameter is BaseException has no narrower static type to dispatch on, so exception classification IS the function and isinstance is the only mechanism Python offers. This arm is load-bearing, not belt-and-braces: InterruptedError is a subclass of OSError, so without this early `return False` the final arm at processor.py:2382 would classify a cooperative-shutdown interrupt as retryable through its OSError member and the RetryManager would keep re-entering the transform during shutdown. The no-retry-manager path spells the identical ordering with `except InterruptedError` at processor.py:2313 ahead of `except (ConnectionError, TimeoutError, OSError, CapacityError)` at :2332. tenacity's own `retry_if_not_exception_type(InterruptedError)` conjunct at retry.py:136 is a second, independent guard living in the caller; this predicate is a named function that must be correct standing alone, and deleting the arm on the strength of the caller's conjunct would leave a function that reports shutdown as retryable to anyone who calls it directly. INVALIDATED BY: InterruptedError ceasing to derive from OSError; OSError being dropped from the 2382 union; this arm being reordered after 2382; or is_retryable acquiring a narrower parameter type that makes the classification statically decidable.

isinstance against an ELSPETH-owned exception base in order to read a per-INSTANCE policy flag. PluginRetryableError (src/elspeth/contracts/errors.py:1497) is ELSPETH's own declared base for plugin errors eligible for engine retry, and its `retryable` bool is set per instance in __init__ (errors.py:1509) — there is no class-level attribute, so the flag is unreachable without first narrowing to the class that defines it. ADR-032 prescribes exactly this nominal form for a type ELSPETH owns. The arm must precede the structural check at processor.py:2382 because the instance flag is the authority: a plugin that raises PluginRetryableError(..., retryable=False) has declared its own failure permanent, and the structural arm below would resurrect it as retryable if the concrete subclass also happened to derive from ConnectionError or OSError. The no-retry-manager path consults the same flag for the same reason at processor.py:2329, choosing reason='transient_error_no_retry' vs 'permanent_error'. INVALIDATED BY: `retryable` becoming a class-level constant or moving off PluginRetryableError; this arm being reordered after 2382; or the engine ceasing to honour a plugin's own permanence declaration.

isinstance against a union of three Python builtins plus one ELSPETH type, as the default arm of the retry predicate. This is the transient-transport classification: the exceptions the engine will spend another attempt on when the plugin did not classify the failure itself via PluginRetryableError. ConnectionError, TimeoutError and OSError are raised by socket, HTTP and filesystem layers underneath third-party SDKs the engine does not own and cannot make declare themselves; there is no owned type to dispatch on and no declaration to consult, so structural type membership is the only signal available at this seam. The union is byte-identical to the `except (ConnectionError, TimeoutError, OSError, CapacityError)` handler at processor.py:2332, which converts the same set to reason='transient_error_no_retry' on the no-retry-manager path — the predicate and that handler are two spellings of one retry policy and are only correct while they stay in lockstep. Correctness of this arm also depends on the two guards above it having already removed InterruptedError (an OSError) and self-classifying PluginRetryableError. INVALIDATED BY: divergence between this union and the 2332 handler tuple; an ELSPETH-owned transport-error base replacing the builtins, which would turn this into owned-type dispatch that should be re-reviewed; or removal/reordering of the InterruptedError and PluginRetryableError arms above.
engine/processor.py:R5:RowProcessor:_rec: isinstance against an ELSPETH-owned abstract base to test a capability before calling it. _record_source_boundary_failure takes `failure: _SourceBoundaryFailure`, the five-member union declared at src/elspeth/engine/processor.py:186-192. Three members (DeclarationContractViolation, AggregateDeclarationContractViolation, PluginContractViolation) subclass AuditEvidenceBase (src/elspeth/contracts/audit_evidence.py:21) and therefore implement to_audit_dict(); FrameworkBugError and OrchestrationInvariantError do not. The narrowing is what lets the function honour the contract stated in its own docstring at processor.py:2496-2499: an evidence-carrying failure contributes its structured to_audit_dict() payload as `context` on BOTH audit writes — the terminal token outcome at processor.py:2525 and the FAILED source node state's ExecutionError at :2544 — while a framework or orchestration bug is still recorded as FAILED but with context=None rather than a fabricated payload. Everything classified here is an ELSPETH-defined exception, so this is owned-type dispatch, not a Tier-3 parse. The alternative structural probe `hasattr(failure, 'to_audit_dict')` is precisely what ADR-032 bans: it is not a security or dispatch control, and any impostor carrying a same-named method would be admitted into the audit context. INVALIDATED BY: to_audit_dict() moving onto a common base of all five union members, which makes the narrowing dead code to delete rather than justify; a union member gaining AuditEvidenceBase whose payload must NOT be written as context; or `context` ceasing to be optional on record_token_outcome and ExecutionError, which would remove the None arm this test selects.

isinstance against a three-tuple of ELSPETH-owned exception classes, selecting the noun used in operator-facing audit-integrity text. `original_label` is consumed only by the two AuditIntegrityError messages raised at src/elspeth/engine/processor.py:2532 and :2552, so an operator reading an audit-write failure sees the right word for what the engine was trying to record. The tuple names exactly the contract-violation members of the _SourceBoundaryFailure union (processor.py:186-192); the remaining two, FrameworkBugError and OrchestrationInvariantError, are failures, not violations. This is deliberately NOT derived from the adjacent audit_context test at processor.py:2505, even though on today's union the two partitions coincide exactly (the same three classes are the AuditEvidenceBase subclasses). 'Carries structured audit evidence' and 'is a contract violation' are distinct properties that happen to agree here; writing this as `if audit_context is not None` would couple operator message wording to an audit-payload concern and would silently mislabel a future union member that is AuditEvidenceBase but not a contract violation. Collapsing the two sites to erase one R5 would be a lint dodge, not a fix — the plan's honest-fix rule forbids exactly that. INVALIDATED BY: a new _SourceBoundaryFailure member that is AuditEvidenceBase but not a contract violation, or a violation class dropped from AuditEvidenceBase — either breaks the coincidence and forces this site and 2505 to be re-reviewed together; or the two AuditIntegrityError messages no longer interpolating original_label, which would make the whole expression dead.
